reasoning_input.question_text: Prove the trigonometric identity: (sin 3θ / sin θ) - (cos 3θ / cos θ) = 2 for θ ≠ kπ/2.

student_steps.content: Combine into single fraction: (sin 3θ cos θ - cos 3θ sin θ) / (sin θ cos θ)
Use compound angle formula: sin(A - B) = sin A cos B - cos A sin B
Use double angle formula: sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ
LHS = (2 sin θ cos θ) / (sin θ cos θ) = 2 = RHS ✓

steps.description: Combine fractions over common denominator sin θ cos θ
steps.expected_expression: (sin 3θ cos θ - cos 3θ sin θ) / (sin θ cos θ)

steps.description: Apply sine compound angle identity to simplify numerator to sin(2θ)
Substitute double angle identity sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ and cancel to prove RHS = 2
steps.expected_expression: (2 sin θ cos θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 2
